reasoning: PRECISE PREMISE CORRECTION (tick 291, live repro): exit 2 here was never an interrupted run. With `-x` (maxfail) AND pytest-xdist the master raises xdist's own `Interrupted(KeyboardInterrupt)` the moment maxfail trips (`xdist/dsession.py: DSession.pytest_runtestloop`), and pytest maps KeyboardInterrupt onto `ExitCode.INTERRUPTED` (2) — so a suite with a REAL failing test exits 2, byte-identical to a signalled run (the same failure without xdist exits 1). Deterministic repro: `pytest -x --tb=short -n 2` over a 3-test synthetic suite with one bad assertion -> exit 2, output ending in `xdist.dsession.Interrupted: stopping after 1 failures`. title: [dogfood:P2] judge tier1's secrets step scans gitreins' OWN state dir, so a persisted guard log containing a QA canary poisons every subsequent verdict with a false FAIL
detail: Observed foreman-side during tick 285 (task DF-GITREINS-POC-16). The first `gitreins task complete` returned Overall FAIL with tier1 secrets passed=false while tier2 PASSed all six criteria and the tests step ran the whole 1529-test suite green. Cause: the judge's default tier1 secrets step runs `gitleaks detect --source . --no-git`, which scans the WHOLE worktree INCLUDING .gitreins/ (its own state dir) and does NOT honour .gitignore in --no-git mode. .gitreins/logs/guard-20260916T161627.314678Z.log — written by the DF-018 full-output persistence — recorded a guard run against the QA battery's 'dogfood-canary3' fixture planted in engine/llm.py:494, and 4 gitleaks findings (rule github-pat / generic-api-key, token ghp_ZQBJP82X43DLLSQT6YP5MSFRHZ6DY9JS7P35(8)) were reproduced by hand from that log. The token is a fake fixture (never in git history; the built-in scanner's test/doc exemption passes) but gitleaks flags it, so tier1 FAILs and no verdict can pass until the debris is deleted. Impact: every judge/task-complete run in this repo is unreliable after any QA-battery or DF-018-era guard run; deleting the log is a workaround, not a fix (the battery recreates it). Fix direction: exclude gitreins' own state from the tier1 secrets scan (.gitreins/** — logs, history, tasks.yaml) in engine/pipeline.py's secrets step, or scan tracked files only, and name the offending path in the step evidence so a FAKE-looking hit is diagnosable without a manual gitleaks run. Repro: plant a ghp_ fixture line in a scratch .gitreins/logs/*.log -> judge tier1 secrets FAIL; remove it -> PASS, nothing else changed.

reasoning.note: Found while verifying DF-GITREINS-POC-16: the judge's own state dir is inside the scan scope of its secrets step, and DF-018 started persisting raw guard output (which legitimately contains fixture secrets from QA canaries) into that scope.

title: P2 — `gitreins guard --full` lint scope ignores the repo's own ruff `extend-exclude`: the whole-tree lint is permanently red on tracked `sandbox/` scratch files (F401/E402), so a full-tree green guard is unreachable and every reader must re-triage the same findings
reasoning: Found live tick 291 while gating INT-FLAKE-2 with the stronger full-mode gate: `gitreins guard --full` -> `Tier 1 Guards: FAIL`, `✗ lint` with F401 (unused `sys`) and two E402 findings, all in `sandbox/test_review.py` — a tracked file that pyproject's `[tool.ruff] extend-exclude` lists (`sandbox/`) precisely so ruff does not grade it. Cause: engine/guard_manager.py builds an explicit file list and invokes `[linter, 'check', *py_files]`; ruff's exclude settings only apply while it recurses into directories, so explicitly-passed excluded files are linted anyway. Consequences: (a) the full-tree lint can never go green (the findings are in intentionally-loose scratch code), (b) the red is not actionable without editing unrelated tracked files, which trains readers to ignore `guard --full`, and (c) it is the same class as the stale-`build/` phantom-E501 trap (a lint finding in a path the repo's own config excludes). title: [P3] MCP protocolVersion is pinned to 2024-11-05 with no negotiation (spec latest is 2026-07-28)
detail: The stdio server answers every initialize with PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2024-11-05" (gitreins_mcp/server.py; extracted into a named constant by the tick-299 DF-GITREINS-POC-5 work), ignoring the client's requested revision. The MCP specification's latest published revision is 2026-07-28 (modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest, read live 2026-09-17), with 2025-03-26 / 2025-06-18 / 2025-11-25 in between; per the spec's version negotiation a server should reply with a revision it supports, so today a modern client asking for 2026-07-28 is told 2024-11-05 and must decide whether to downgrade — and the docs advertise '2024-11-05' as the protocol because that is all the server knows. Acceptance: the server advertises the newest revision it actually implements in SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS, echoes the client's requested revision when supported (else answers with its own newest and records the mismatch on stderr), tests cover a supported request, an unrecognized request, and an absent protocolVersion, and docs/mcp-api.md + docs/cli-reference.md name the negotiated value instead of a constant.
why: Found while making the MCP identity truthful (DF-GITREINS-POC-5 item 2): the version a client reasons about now agrees with the release, but the protocol revision it negotiates against is several spec revisions stale and is not negotiable at all.
worker_summary: foreman-direct (tick 305, PLUS ULTRA endgame sweep)
foreman_note: DELIVERED: gitreins_mcp/server.py now negotiates. SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = (2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05) — every revision sharing the initialize handshake and the tools-only surface this stdio server implements — and PROTOCOL_VERSION is its newest member. initialize echoes a supported request; anything else (2026-07-28, a typo, or no value at all) is answered with 2025-11-25 plus one stderr line naming the mismatch and the revisions a client may retry with, with the server/discover fallback spelled out. 2026-07-28 is deliberately NOT advertised (verified against modelcontextprotocol.io: it removed the initialize handshake, made MCP stateless, moved the version into each request's _meta and made server/discover mandatory). title: [P3] A structurally truncated .gitreins/tasks.yaml loads as a silent PARTIAL task list (rc=0, no warning) instead of reporting corruption
detail: Probe (tick 303, scratch copy of the repo at HEAD, `.venv/bin/gitreins task list`): with the intact 76,881-byte store the command lists 119 task lines; with the file truncated to its first 40 bytes it exits 0 and prints ONE bogus task ('○ v0.4.1-model-fix  V') with NO warning; with 200 bytes of NUL/random garbage it prints 'Warning: failed to load tasks: <utf-8 decode error>' and 'No tasks found.' So the store has an integrity signal only for DECODE failures: `TaskManager._load` catches every exception with a printed warning (engine/task_manager.py:53-72) but a truncation that still parses as YAML yields a plausible-looking, silently wrong task set — the same 'corrupted state must fail loudly' class as QA-GITREINS-POC-6, one layer in. Impact is diagnostic rather than destructive (a mutation on the bogus id fails with 'Task not found'), and the fix direction is a structural check rather than a new dependency: validate that the parsed doc is a mapping whose `tasks` is a list of mappings carrying `id`, and when the file is non-empty but yields zero tasks, say so explicitly instead of printing an empty list. Related: the tick-304 lane's in-repo corrupted-state work (commit 764240f) covers the write/destroy side; this row is the read side, so treat it as a companion and close it as duplicate if that arc already covers partial reads.
reasoning: Found while verifying QA-GITREINS-POC-6's class in-repo (the QA battery asks 'clean failure or recovery after corruption?'). Filed with the exact probe and the fix direction; no code was changed for it in this tick.

Repro confirmed exactly as filed in a scratch repo at HEAD with a copy of the live 79950-byte store: intact -> 120 tasks, no warning; first 40 bytes -> rc 0, ONE bogus task ('v0.4.1-model-fix'), no warning, no preserved sidecar; 200 NUL bytes -> loud warning + preserved sidecar. title: P2 — a Tier 2 response with trailing data after the verdict JSON degrades to INCOMPLETE with an EMPTY item list: `_parse_verdict` slices first-`{`..last-`}` (greedy), then the keyword fallback keeps only `content[:300]`, so the verdict artifact cannot say which criterion failed
detail: Tick 306, GR-GAP-055 (release v0.14.0): `gitreins task complete` printed 'gitreins.evaluator: WARNING: JSON parse failed: Extra data: line 1 column 4252 (char 4251)' and then 'Falling back to keyword parse: verdict=INCOMPLETE'. The artifact `.gitreins/history/2026-09-18/91176df2/verdict.json` records `passed: false`, top-level `items: []`, and stage tier2 summary 'INCOMPLETE\n\n(auto-parsed from non-JSON response) {"verdict":"INCOMPLETE",...' truncated mid-item, so the per-criterion result was LOST: the reader cannot tell which criterion the model failed. Cause (engine/evaluator.py:1896-1945): Strategy 2 takes `cleaned[find('{') : rfind('}')+1]`, so any response that carries a second `}` after the object (trailing note, echoed example, duplicated object) is handed to `json.loads` as one over-long slice and raises 'Extra data' — the classic fix is `json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(cleaned, start)` to take the FIRST complete object and ignore the tail. Strategy 3 then discards the model's own items and keeps `content[:300]` in `summary`. FIX: raw_decode first-object parsing + preserve the model's items (or the parse error) in the verdict record so a parse hiccup can never masquerade as a criterion failure. title: [P1] loadgen.py is unbounded: no max-procs, no teardown, orphans outlive the run - locked the host for hours (2026-09-18)
detail: loadgen.py spawns `timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c while :; do :; done` units from a for-loop with NO cap on count and NO teardown on interruption. Measured consequence 2026-09-18 on karaHermes-mde-7840hs: 278 concurrent null-loop units, loadavg 220-346, ~2000 processes, unusable host; the units were adopted by `systemd --user` (PPID = user manager) after their spawner exited, so a killed or crashed judge leaves its load RUNNING. Repeated evaluator runs respawn the load. REQUIRED: --max-procs (default 4-8, hard ceiling), unit lifetime cap (<=30s, not 300), try/finally + signal handlers (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP) that kill the whole process group, an abort path that proves zero survivors, and a 'load class' marker so evaluators can serialize instead of stacking. Also: the judge should refuse/skip a load-class criterion when host loadavg already exceeds a threshold, recording SKIPPED with the reason (never a silent bare FAIL). Evidence: /tmp/reap_forkbomb.py run, ~/.hermes/logs/forkbomb-reaper.jsonl, snoopy exec trace 2026-09-18 15:40 cwd:/home/kara/crier.  CORRECTION (same day, after reading the code): `scripts/loadgen.py` is NOT the emitter — it is the already-correct replacement (bounded workers MAX_WORKERS=8, capped seconds, PR_SET_PDEATHSIG so children die with the runner, refuses to run on a shared host, fails the run if any child survives; its own docstring documents an earlier 33.8-loadavg incident). The actual emitter is AD-HOC, AGENT-AUTHORED shell: agents hand-rolled `for i in $(seq 1 N); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` as a 'load the box' step, with no teardown, so the units were orphaned to systemd --user and outlived every caller. state.db evidence spans multiple projects and weeks: Kobayashi-Maru (2026-08-25), ring-runner, crier. FIX LANDED 2026-09-18 by Kara-agent: the terminal-jail plugin now VETOES this class at the tool boundary (pre_tool_call -> {"action":"block","message"}) via terminal_jail/spin_policy.py (busy-wait loops, unbounded yes/cat /dev/zero/dd, shell fork bombs; 5/5 tests pass; override HERMES_TERMINAL_JAIL_ALLOW_SPIN=1). So this row's remaining scope is NOT 'bound loadgen' (already bounded) but: (1) make loadgen the easy path for agents (a discoverable wrapper + AGENTS.md pointer), (2) audit remaining harnesses/scripted repros for the old idiom, (3) keep the host reaper as backstop.  ROOT CAUSE FOUND (code level, 2026-09-18 evening): the emitter is GitReins' OWN tier-2 evaluator. `engine/evaluator.py::_tool_run_command` ran the judge's shell as `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, timeout=...)` — `timeout=` reaps only the DIRECT child, so any BACKGROUNDED children escape: a command like `for i in $(seq 1 64); do timeout 300 nice -n 0 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' & done` (the idiom the judge invents when a criterion demands 'fails on a loaded box') leaves every unit running, reparented to `systemd --user`. Measured: 278 orphans, loadavg 220-346. ps chain proved the path: `gitreins task complete DF-CRIER-252` → the for-loop shell → the burners (a direct child of the gitreins process, which is why no Hermes session/tool-call record exists and why the terminal-jail veto does NOT cover it — the host reaper was the only backstop). Amplifiers: the tier-2 stage is budgeted at 400 iterations / 30m / 48M input tokens (crier/.gitreins/config.yaml), so a judge run is long and can issue many commands; crier's own criteria (e.g. QA-CRIER-17: '20+ consecutive go test ./cmd/server -count=1 runs are green') legitimately push the judge toward load-bearing verification. FIX LANDED: new `engine/command_hygiene.py` — (a) refuses busy-wait/unbounded-burn/fork-bomb commands with a message naming `sleep` and `scripts/loadgen.py`; (b) spawns every command with `start_new_session=True` and reaps the WHOLE process group on timeout AND on normal exit (validated pgid: never PID 1, group must exist in /proc, survivors are reported in the tool result rather than hidden). Wired into `_tool_run_command` and `pipeline._run_script_step`. Tests: `tests/test_command_hygiene.py`, 20 passing behaviour tests (backgrounded child reaped on normal exit; timeout kills the group; refusal proven by side effect). Deploy step: the lanes run the pipx copy at ~/.local/share/pipx/venvs/gitreins (installed from file:///home/kara/gitreins-poc), so it must be reinstalled from the repo for the fix to reach them.

title: P3 - the tier-2 compaction valve cannot fire on a rung larger than ~10x the model window: it compares the LARGEST SINGLE PROMPT against compaction_threshold x max_input_tokens while the cap meters the SUM over calls, so a large rung leaves the valve dead config and the input cap a hard wall
detail: Measured 2026-09-19 by get-h3/sdk-python foreman tick #300 while settling that repo's tier-2 rung (its GAP-057). MECHANISM (lines read in this repo): the proactive valve in engine/evaluator.py compares `cumulative_prompt_tok = max(cumulative_prompt_tok, prompt_tok)` — the LARGEST SINGLE CALL's prompt — against `threshold = int(self.eval_cap.max_input_tokens * evaluator_cfg.get('compaction_threshold', 0.90))`, a share of the CUMULATIVE budget, while the cap itself meters the SUM over calls (engine/eval_cap.py `record_llm_call` -> `cumulative_input_tokens += all_input`, checked in `_check_hard_caps`). The comparison's semantics are pinned by this repo's own regression tests: tests/test_evaluator.py::test_compaction_threshold_config_override fires compaction on a SINGLE 600-token call against a 1,000-token cap at ratio 0.50, and ::test_compaction_threshold_not_triggered_below shows a 400-token call against a 10,000-token cap NOT firing. CONSEQUENCE at fleet rungs: on any config whose max_input_tokens is much larger than a single prompt (the fleet runs 2M-24M), the valve can never fire, compaction is unreachable, `reset_context_tracking` never runs and the input counter only grows — measured on the h3 repo: an instrumented 41-call run peaked at a 46,391-token single prompt (P0=3,831 + 1,064 tokens/call) against the then-1M rung, recorded 0 compactions and died at 1,029,521 cumulative tokens; the ratio that WOULD fire at that peak is 0.023 at a 2M rung and 0.006 at 8M. So the config-only 'fix' is a magic number read off one task's growth law, and it also thrashes: a tool-heavy run adding ~5K tokens/call crosses a 46K trigger in ~5 calls, burning the engine's 3-compaction allowance (MAX_COMPACTIONS) before the first criterion is verified. FIX (engine, either): (a) compare the quantity the cap enforces — `self.eval_cap.cumulative_input_tokens > threshold` — so the valve fires at the configured share of the budget and compaction resets the budget it was designed to protect; or (b) split the knob into an explicit context-window knob (compared against an estimated context size) and an explicit budget-share knob, so no config can express a valve that cannot fire. Whichever is chosen, the README/CHANGELOG must say WHICH quantity the ratio multiplies. PASS: on a config whose max_input_tokens dwarfs a single prompt (e.g. 8M with a ~50K peak prompt) a live eval records a compaction event at the configured ratio, the reset is visible in .gitreins/usage.jsonl as a numerically smaller later line, and a regression test asserts the valve fires on cumulative consumption rather than on one call's prompt size.

Every fleet repo that has raised max_input_tokens above the model window now carries a dead safety valve and a hard wall, and the failure reads as 'config missing' to each consumer in turn, so it gets re-derived per project until it is fixed here. title: P2 - bunker-qa.sh launch: three zero-battery failure modes, all reported as success (tool-cap kill mid-sync; CAP_KB unbound ships 0-byte qa-run.sh; no post-launch liveness verification)
reasoning:
Harness finding from the 2026-09-20 gitreins-poc dogfood install leg — 3 consecutive launch attempts died with ZERO battery execution, each by a different mechanism. The driver reported "launch complete" every time; only direct agent probes showed nothing had run. Filed here because bunker-qa.sh is shared fleet harness (owning repo workdir), not a gitreins defect.

MECHANISMS (all three reproducible):
1. `bunker-qa.sh launch` synchronous mode killed at the Hermes tool cap (~240-420s) mid `sync_repo` (513MB tree): spawn + partial sync done, qa-run.sh NEVER shipped, no cells recorded, launcher dies with the tool call. Evidence: agent 8ef8b876 + later 70bc1d49 had ~/qa-gitreins-poc partial trees, no ~/qa-run.sh, no qa-logs.
2. With CAP_KB unset: `bunker-qa.sh launch` prints `line 327: CAP_KB: unbound variable` (set -u) INSIDE build_remote_script's heredoc — the generated script is shipped 0 BYTES — and launch() then still prints "QA launch complete". Evidence: agent aea901ba, qa-run.sh = 0 bytes (verified via ssh), empty evidence file. detect_cmds() sets DETECT_INSTALL/DETECT_NATIVE but never CAP_KB; CAP_KB=3145728 lives at line 800 (run()-path default). Workaround used: `CAP_KB=3145728 bunker-qa.sh launch ...`.
3. Even with CAP_KB exported, sync_repo (513MB gitreins tree over tailscale) + tar exceeds the ~420s tool cap before the script ships. launch() needs to either stream the sync in background itself, or the driver needs a --skip-sync + manual-rsync escape.

CONSEQUENCE CLASS: "launch complete + LAUNCH_RC=0" is NOT proof a battery is running (echoes the 09-16 off-by-one "filed:N is not proof" lesson, one layer up the stack). Post-launch verification MUST probe the agent for qa-run.sh non-empty + a live process before walking away.

FIX DIRECTION: build_remote_script defines CAP_KB locally (one line) or drops it from the generation-time substitution; launch() verifies shipped script size >0 and a running pid before printing success; document the tool-cap incompatibility for big repos.

title: JEV-RESOLUTION core: engine/resolution.py — trace a question through the Hilo graph, assemble the answering code inside a measured token budget, return a calibrated resolution probability from Jev with fail-closed bands
detail:
SPEC: docs/jev-resolution-gate.md (design authority — read it before designing the module).
GOAL: given a question (task acceptance criteria / judge criterion / free-form agent question), answer 'is the code we can point at sufficient to resolve this — and if not, what kind of piece is missing?' as a TYPED, cheap (~$0.0003-$0.0012), calibrated decision instead of an open-ended LLM read.

PIPELINE: (1) TRACE via hilo graph search -> graph related --direction reverse (the path, not a haystack); (2) ASSEMBLE via hilo graph understand --budget 16000, extra targeted bundles per seed while budget remains, bounded line-aligned reads only as last resort; (3) BUDGET: measure the text, enforce MAX_BUNDLE_TOKENS=28000, clip line-aligned and DISCLOSE. TOKEN ESTIMATE: do NOT use a fixed chars/3.5 divisor — the same filler family measured 1.98 chars/token (repetitive) and 3.5 chars/token (varied), so chars/3.5 undercounts by up to ~75% and blows the ceiling. Use a real tokenizer when available, else the conservative floor chars//2; recompute after each bundle and record the measurement in the verdict. MEASURED CEILING: 32,778 in-tokens accepted at 65,000 chars; 30,008 accepted at 105,160 chars; rejected above ~33k with HTTP 400 max_tokens_exceeded the omission — REUSE engine/evidence_bounds.py, do NOT write a second truncator; (4) ONE Jev call with three typed questions (resolves_question=noul, missing_kind=choice, evidence_quality=score); (5) BANDS in code: >=0.85 RESOLVED, >=0.50 REVIEW, <0.50 UNRESOLVED, ANY transport/auth/malformed failure -> ABSTAIN and exit non-zero (FAIL CLOSED).

OUTPUT must carry: probability, verdict band, missing_kind, evidence_quality, the bundle MANIFEST (file -> provenance, score, bytes, truncated?), model build id echoed by the API, token counts and cost. A verdict without a traceable bundle is not a verdict.

KEY HANDLING: try every sk-or-v1-* candidate found in the env and the known .env locations, moving on for 401/402/429 (precedent: ~/guard/jev.go loadOpenRouterKeys); never log a key; all candidates dead -> ABSTAIN, never a silent RESOLVED.

TESTS: hermetic (mock the decisions endpoint) for bands, budget clipping, disclosure, failover and fail-closed; plus a live smoke run whose output is pasted into the row's foreman_note.

MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-20 (reference values, re-verify before trusting): Jev = POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions, model typesafe/jev-1.13 (a DECISIONS model; /chat/completions returns 400). Answers are TYPED: noul (0-1 prob) | choice (label+probs) | score (rubric pos). Several questions answered in ONE request for one flat cost. Cost measured: 315 in-tokens -> $0.0000132 ; 30,008 in-tokens -> $0.001260336 (=$0.042/M in, $0 out). INPUT CEILING measured: 30,008 in-tokens ACCEPTED, ~30.2k+ REJECTED with HTTP 400 max_tokens_exceeded -> usable budget ~30k, spec caps the bundle at 28k tokens. chars/token ~= 3.5. Discrimination proven: a real snippet scored noul 0.87 while 30k tokens of filler scored 0.09. KEYS: GITREINS_OPENROUTER_KEY LIVE; OPENROUTER_API_KEY is 401 EXPIRED -> failover across ALL sk-or-v1-* candidates is mandatory. Hilo assembly: `hilo graph understand "<task>" --budget N` emits ## MAP / ## SIGNATURES / ## DETAIL with real whitespace-minified source plus per-file provenance+score; `hilo graph search "<q>" --limit N` gives ranked seeds (TF-IDF+BM25, deterministic); `hilo graph related <f> --direction reverse` gives the dependency path. HILO CAVEATS: --budget is a COARSE TIER not a hard clip (2000/4000/8000 all returned the same 8,889 chars; 16000-30000 returned 41,242 chars); one bundle on this repo caps at ~41k chars (~11.8k Jev tokens) so broad questions need multi-bundle assembly or bounded reads; `graph stats` is NOT JIT (empty on cold cache) while related/impact ARE JIT.

title: JEV-RESOLUTION calibration harness: labeled resolved/unresolved corpus + threshold sweep, so the 0.85/0.50 bands are measured rather than guessed
detail:
SPEC: docs/jev-resolution-gate.md sect. 3.5/8. DEPENDS on JEVRES-001.
WHY: every threshold in this design (0.85 RESOLVED, 0.50 REVIEW, 28k token ceiling) is a starting guess. The injection-guard precedent in this fleet showed the real failure mode is *calibration drift between model builds* and *false positives on quoted/adjacent content* — both only visible against a labeled set.

BUILD: a corpus of (question, repo-state, ground truth) cases where ground truth is INDEPENDENTLY established, not asserted by the resolver:
  - resolved: land a real fix, then ask the question its acceptance criteria describe.
  - unresolved: ask before the fix (and keep the pair, so the same question is measured in both states — that pairing is the actual signal).
  - near-miss negatives: the code MENTIONS the topic but does not implement it (the analogue of the guard's quote-context false positive); a test exists but does not cover the behaviour; the implementation exists but is not wired.
  - budget-starved: a genuine answer that does not fit in 28k tokens — must surface as 'budget exhausted', NOT as UNRESOLVED (different failure, different fix).

DELIVERABLE: `scripts/jevres_calibrate.py` + a checked-in corpus; prints a confusion matrix over a threshold sweep and fails loudly if the chosen bands regress. Hermetic mode (mock endpoint) for CI + a live mode for real calibration. Record the model build id with results.

title: P3 - a resumed MCP evaluation job re-persists a SECOND verdict entry sharing the same job_id — .gitreins/history can hold two records for one logical run
reasoning:
Found 2026-09-20 by the gitreins-poc foreman while closing DF-GITREINS-POC-23 (the fix that made MCP runs persist at all — before it, nothing was written, so this gap could not exist).

MECHANISM: gitreins_mcp/server.py `_resume_disk_job` re-dispatches an orphaned `running` job (server restarted / worker died) through `_start_job_thread` with the SAME job record, so `job['id']` is unchanged; `_run_job` now calls persist_evaluation(extra={'job_id': job['id'], 'source': 'mcp'}) on every terminal `complete`, and VerdictPersister keys the history entry on timestamp+task id, not on the job id. A resume therefore writes a second `<date>/<hash>/verdict.json` that carries the SAME job_id as the first — two verdict records for one logical run, distinguishable only by their evaluated_at/hash.

WHY IT MATTERS: `job_id` is the cross-reference the DF-GITREINS-POC-23 record introduced so a browsable verdict can be tied back to the job that produced it. After a resume that key is no longer unique, so a consumer joining history to the job store cannot tell which record is the graded result and which is a re-run; the judge spend of the abandoned attempt is also not labelled as superseded.

EVIDENCE / REPRO: dispatch an MCP task.complete, SIGKILL the server process while the job is `running` (~mid tier1), then poll judge.status on a fresh server: the resume path runs the evaluation again (tests/test_mcp_server.py::test_orphaned_running_job_is_resumed_on_status covers the resume) and, with persistence wired, two history entries appear for one job id. The existing tests assert one verdict per dispatch, so the resume arm is unpinned.

FIX DIRECTION (either): (a) stamp a resume counter / `attempt` in the record and make the job_id key unique by (job_id, attempt); or (b) have the persister supersede instead of append when a record with the same job_id already exists (mark the older one superseded, or reuse its entry). Add a test that resumes a job with persistence enabled and asserts exactly ONE live record per job id. Re-verify DF-GITREINS-POC-24's poll predicate at the same time (it is the same resume surface).
worker_summary: A resumed MCP evaluation job no longer leaves two live verdict records for one job_id: engine/persist.py supersedes the interrupted entry (approach (b)) - before writing, the persister finds the newest LIVE entry for that job id, stamps the new record with supersedes and labels the old one superseded_by/superseded_at via tmp+os.replace, never raising on bookkeeping. Superseding labels, never deletes: the abandoned attempt keeps its evidence. Records without a job_id (sync surfaces) and different job ids are never superseded. 3 new tests (14 -> 17 in test_mcp_verdict_persistence.py) fabricate the exact crash window - an orphaned running job with a dead pid plus one real persist - then poll judge.status so the server resumes; all three were RED against the pre-fix persister. title: P1 - a fresh venv install where pytest is not installed makes `gitreins guard` FAIL the tests lane with `/bin/sh: 1: pytest: not found`, and that FAIL blocks the README's own 'Try the hook' first commit - the venv-local binary is the only gitreins on the command line, yet the guard subprocess cannot see the venv's pytest
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-20b dogfood on las-bunker-03 agent 3f4f7cdc (fresh Debian 13, rootless docker, no toolchains), wheel 0.14.0 from PyPI.

REPRO (all on the fresh box, `~/app`, after the README quickstart):
  python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install gitreins   # 32s, OK
  .venv/bin/gitreins install && .venv/bin/gitreins init     # writes test_mode: full, test_command: "pytest -x --tb=short"
  .venv/bin/gitreins guard
    Tier 1 Guards: FAIL  (test mode: full)
      ~ lint - skipped (no linter on PATH)
      x tests (full) - /bin/sh: 1: pytest: not found
    GUARD_EXIT=1
  git commit -m "test"     # the README's documented next step
    COMMIT_EXIT=1           # the pre-commit hook re-runs the same FAIL and BLOCKS the commit

THE BIN WE INVOKED LIVES IN THE VENV THAT OWNS pyTEST, SO THE FAILURE IS PURE PATH PROPAGATION, NOT A MISSING DEP: after `./.venv/bin/pip install pytest` the same command run as `./.venv/bin/gitreins guard` STILL fails `pytest: not found` (the guard shells out via `sh -c` with the ambient PATH), while `source .venv/bin/activate && gitreins guard` succeeds: `Tier 1: DEGRADED PASS (skips: lint=no linter on PATH)`, `v tests (full)`, GUARD_EXIT=0, and the hook commit then lands (COMMIT_EXIT=0, 7 files). So the user-visible difference between 'works' and 'your first documented commit is blocked' is whether they activated the venv - a fact no doc mentions and the error message does not hint at.

WHY IT MATTERS: the README's own onboarding path is `pip install` -> `install` -> `init` -> 'Try the hook: make a change, git add ., git commit -m test'. On a fresh machine the FIRST such commit exits 1 with a message that names a tool the user believes they installed. Nothing distinguishes 'your environment is wrong' from 'your code is broken'. The engine already has the right pattern here - the documented uv/pipenv/poetry fallback rewrites the runner when the configured runner's binary is missing - it just does not extend to the interpreter that launched gitreins.

ALSO MEASURED, SAME LEG (pre-existing, recorded as context not as a new defect): the README's literal `pip install gitreins` is impossible on fresh Debian (PEP 668, exit 1, 'externally-managed-environment'); the venv path is the only one that works and is documented only as a *source-checkout* note.

FIX DIRECTION: resolve the test command against the interpreter/venv that runs gitreins (sys.executable's bindir prepended to the subprocess PATH) exactly as the runner-fallback logic already rewrites `uv run pytest`; failing that, detect `command not found` and print the actionable line ('pytest is not on PATH - activate the venv that has it, or set guards.test_command'). Add a regression that runs guard from an unactivated venv with pytest installed only there.
reasoning: This is the first-60-seconds experience of the documented quickstart, and it ends in a blocked commit with a misleading error - the same class the 0.14.0 release notes claim closed for the case where the harness knows the runner is missing.

title: P1 - `gitreins qa record` with neither --verdict nor --exit-code writes `verdict: UNKNOWN / status: unknown`, contradicting its own docs ('a passing verdict when neither is given') - the QA-lane row lands in the fleet ledger as neither pass nor fail
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-20b dogfood (QA-ledger angle). docs/cli-reference.md:586-590 states: '`--project` defaults to the repository directory name, `--kind` to `lane`, `--verdict`/`--exit-code` to a passing verdict when neither is given, and `--commit` to the repository's `HEAD`.'

MEASURED (HEAD via .venv, and independently on the 0.14.0 wheel inside the fresh bunker agent - a controlled run, with the config confirmed to contain `qa_ledger:\n  enabled: true` and no residual flags):
  $ gitreins qa record --kind lane --note CONTROLLED-DEFAULT
  qa ledger: recorded lane <repo> UNKNOWN in <repo>/.gitreins/qa-ledger.jsonl
  REAL_EXIT=0
  {"ts":"...","project":"...","status":"unknown","verdict":"UNKNOWN","kind":"lane","cells":{},"findings":[],"evidence":"","note":"CONTROLLED-DEFAULT",...}
Command and hook bodies are non-empty (no stray shell expansion): the earlier stray UNKNOWNs in the same scratch ledger were emitted while the hook had accidentally flipped `history.enabled` instead of `qa_ledger.enabled`, and a later controlled run reproduced UNKNOWN cleanly.

WHY IT MATTERS, IN THIS FLEET SPECIFICALLY: the documented consumer of `qa record` is 'a run produced outside the harness (a fleet lane, a bunker battery)' - and the real commands this fleet used on 2026-09-19/20 passed the verdict explicitly (`qa record ... --verdict FAIL --exit-code 1 --cell ci-pass=FAIL`). A lane that omits it - the natural reading of 'defaults to a passing verdict' - writes a row that `qa list` renders with neither a tick nor a cross, so a green battery and an undecided one are indistinguishable in the ledger the judgment browser reads. `status` and `verdict` are both the string UNKNOWN, so no consumer can tell 'not decided' from 'decision lost'.

reasoning: The QA ledger is the newest surface (0.14.0) and its whole purpose is to be the harness record of what QA actually did - a row that reads UNKNOWN defeats the audit, and the fleet's own lanes are the documented consumers.

title: P1 - `gitreins commit-audit` is a silent no-op unless the user hand-writes a pipeline stage, and the documented `mode: block` placement is not the one the engine reads: a stage-level `mode: block` stays a warning with exit 0, while only a TOP-LEVEL `commit_audit:` block actually blocks
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-20b dogfood (commit-msg hook angle: docs/cli-reference.md' Hooks section ships the hook snippet but no body - prior runs never exercised the audit).

FOUR MEASUREMENTS, one scratch repo, wheel-equivalent HEAD CLI:
1. NO pipeline stage (the state after `gitreins install` + `init`): `gitreins commit-audit "wip"` -> exit 0, STDOUT empty, STDERR empty. Same for a perfect message and for one carrying the `gitreins.skip-tier2` trailer. The command prints NOTHING and audits NOTHING; the docs promise 'Validate a commit message against staged diff' and the README lists commit audit among the standing surface. `engine/pipeline.py:253` builds the stage list from `config['pipeline']['stages']`, which no installer path ever writes.
2. STAGE DECLARED (`pipeline.stages[] = {id: commit_audit, type: commit_audit, on: [commit-msg], mode: warn}`): the audit runs and is genuinely good - it rejected 'wip' with two specific reasons and a suggested message. So the capability works; only the activation path is undocumented.
3. STAGE-LEVEL `mode: block` (the placement docs/cli-reference.md implies - 'only when the config's pipeline includes a commit_audit stage with commit_audit.mode: block'): STILL exit 0 and '(Warning only - commit will proceed)'. The block flag is ignored.
4. TOP-LEVEL `commit_audit: {mode: block}`: exit 1 and '(Commit BLOCKED - fix message or set commit_audit.mode=warn)'. This is the only placement that blocks.

ROOT CAUSE (read, not guessed): `engine/pipeline.py:_load_commit_audit_config` (line ~862-871) loads the yaml and returns `cfg.get("commit_audit", {})` - TOP LEVEL ONLY. The stage dict's own `mode` key is never consulted, so the documented stage-scoped placement is dead config, and `defaults.commit_audit.mode: block` (the natural place given every other setting lives under `defaults:`) is dead too - measured, still exit 0.

WHY IT MATTERS: a user who follows the doc creates the hook, sets 'mode: block' where the doc says, and believes their commits are gated by message audit. They are not: every message passes with exit 0. And in the default state the hook is pure overhead that prints nothing at all - a false sense of a gate on both ends.

FIX DIRECTION: resolve `mode` with an explicit precedence (stage > defaults.commit_audit > top-level > warn) and document the one that wins; when no pipeline stage matches the trigger, print a named skip line ('commit audit: no pipeline stage with type commit_audit for trigger commit-msg - audit NOT run') instead of silently exiting 0. Regression: a stage-level block blocks, and a stage-less run says so.
reasoning: The command is advertised in the README standing surface and has a doc section, but in the documented configuration it silently does nothing and in the documented 'block' configuration it silently fails to block - the worst pair for a quality gate, because both failure directions look like success.

A stage-less run prints a named skip (commit_audit_skip_message) instead of exiting 0 in silence. Live E2E verified by the foreman on the merged tree: cases A(stage block)->exit 1, B(no stage)->named skip, C(top-level block, no stage)->skip (same exit 0 as pre-fix, now named), D(stage warn beats top-level block)->warn, E(stage no mode + top-level block)->exit 1 (backward compat), F(defaults.commit_audit block)->exit 1 (previously dead config). +18 tests (test_commit_audit.py 81->99), 16 RED-proven against the unfixed engine.

title: P2 - `gitreins install` does not gitignore the QA ledger it ships, so a routine `git add -A && git commit` commits fleet QA rows (agent ids, server names, evidence paths, findings) into the user's history
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-20b dogfood on the fresh bunker agent, wheel 0.14.0.

MEASURED: in a plain repo after `gitreins install`, the `.gitignore` entries written are exactly: `.gitreins/tasks.yaml`, `.gitreins/config.yaml.bak`, `.gitreins/usage.jsonl`, `.gitreins/logs/`. `git check-ignore .gitreins/qa-ledger.jsonl` -> exit 1 (not ignored) in that fresh repo, grep for 'qa-ledger' in its .gitignore -> 0 matches. Then `git add -A && git commit -m "test"` succeeded and its summary listed `create mode 100644 .gitreins/qa-ledger.jsonl` among the 7 files changed.

WHY IT IS A REGRESSION CLASS RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT: the ledger line EXISTS in gitreins' own `.gitignore` (line 31, with a comment: 'runtime artifact. Point GITREINS_QA_LEDGER at a tracked path to version it.') and it was added by `67eca8f` - the SAME commit that introduced the feature (`feat(qa): record QA run outcomes in a harness QA ledger`, which the log trail confirms also touched .gitignore). So the ignore was applied to the vendor checkout only; the installer's gitignore template was not updated, and the vendor repo is the one place it is not needed.

WHY IT MATTERS: ledger rows are not neutral - a row carries `agent`, `server`, `evidence` (often a bunker/agent path), `findings` (ids and titles), and `commit`. Committing them leaks fleet infrastructure details into a user's public history and, worse, makes the ledger a tracked file whose later rewrites/dedupes look like content edits. The documented intent is the opposite ('runtime artifact; point GITREINS_QA_LEDGER at a tracked path to version it'), i.e. opting IN to versioning.

FIX DIRECTION: ship `.gitreins/qa-ledger.jsonl` in the install-time gitignore template (single source: the same list the repo already maintains), and cover it with a test that asserts every runtime artifact the ledger module writes is ignored after `gitreins install`.

title: P2 - the QA ledger's own rotation silently drops rows at max_entries and the command reports success: 3 rows at max_entries=3, a 4th record exits 0 ('recorded') and the count stays 3
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-20b dogfood (QA-ledger angle).

MEASURED in the scratch consumer: ledger held 3 rows with `qa_ledger.max_entries: 3` in .gitreins/config.yaml (which the ledger module honours - the newest 3 were retained, the older ones dropped, as docs/cli-reference.md documents: 'qa_ledger.max_entries (default 1000) keeps the newest rows').
  $ gitreins qa record --kind lane --note ROW4
  qa ledger: recorded lane <repo> UNKNOWN in <repo>/.gitreins/qa-ledger.jsonl
  EXIT=0     # and the row count on disk is still exactly 3
Retention itself is correct and tested; what is not surfaced is that a record can evict another record, so an append-only audit trail silently loses its oldest entry while every write reports success.

WHY IT MATTERS (honest scope): default max_entries is 1000, so a single repo reaches this rarely - this is a P2, not a P1. It becomes material for the documented fleet use ('point GITREINS_QA_LEDGER at a fleet ledger to append there'): one shared fleet ledger with many projects mutating it, plus a rotation policy that discards the oldest rows without a word, means the fleet's QA history can be silently truncated by whoever writes next, and no consumer can tell how many rows were lost. Combined with DF-GITREINS-POC-29 (rows can be written as UNKNOWN) and DF-GITREINS-POC-31 (the ledger is not gitignored on install), the row store has three independent ways to be wrong about what happened.

FIX DIRECTION: report eviction on stderr when a record pushes the ledger past max_entries (name the count evicted, mirroring the DEGRADED-pass naming convention the guard already uses); consider counting lifetime rows in a header/first-row metadata field so a truncated ledger remains interpretable. Regression: record past the cap and assert the eviction is announced.
reasoning: Low severity today, high severity in the fleet configuration the docs actively recommend (a shared ledger path), where silent truncation is indistinguishable from 'no such run'.
worker_summary: QA-ledger rotation is no longer silent: _prune returns the dropped-row count and append_row — the single choke point every writer shares (qa record CLI, worktree fresh/repro/dogfood) — prints `qa ledger: rotation evicted N row(s) (max_entries=M)` to stderr when a record pushes the ledger past the cap. stdout is byte-identical (consumers unaffected); no eviction line on the happy path. Foreman live replay on the merged tree: 3 rows at max_entries=3 -> 4th record exit 0, eviction line on stderr, newest 3 retained. +2 tests, RED-proven.

title: P1 - two Tier-1 timing assertions in tests/test_mcp_server.py flake under load and turn a correct commit's judge verdict into Overall FAIL (`assert elapsed < 1.0` / `assert elapsed < 0.5`)
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-21 foreman tick (wave of 3, DF-GITREINS-POC-30).

MEASURED: `gitreins task complete DF-GITREINS-POC-30` returned Overall FAIL with `tier2 PASS (6/6 ACs)` and `tier1 FAIL` — the sole failing step was `tests/test_mcp_server.py::TestJudgeAsyncMCP::test_judge_evaluate_async_returns_immediately` (line 803: `assert elapsed < 1.0`), on the merged tree dcbbbc0.

FLAKE PROOF (not assumed): on rerun the SAME commit's judge failed a DIFFERENT timing test of the same class — `TestJudgeAsyncMCP::test_task_complete_dispatches_async_job_when_llm_configured` (`assert elapsed < 0.5`, got 1.29s) — in a file whose diff vs the previous merge is EMPTY. The first test passes in isolation (0.46s), under xdist contention (0.63-0.76s), and under single-core saturation; GitHub CI on the same commit runs the full suite GREEN on py3.10/3.11/3.12 (run 35564727432).

WHY IT MATTERS: the judge ran the full suite while other heavy runs shared the host (8 concurrent `gitreins task complete` processes observed). A wall-clock ceiling near the busy-host mean makes an otherwise-correct commit read as a regression to whoever reads the verdict, and it burns a second ~10-min judge run to discover the flake. Off-by-One class 1405 (typescript-test-perf-threshold-flake) already documents the fix pattern for exactly this: do not invent a new number — reuse a file-owned, CI-generous constant and base it on the measured busy-host distribution, not the idle-workstation one.

FIX DIRECTION: raise both ceilings to a file-owned CI_GENEROUS-style constant (the file already uses a generous async-wait value elsewhere) and, where the assertion only needs to prove 'did not block', assert against the stub's own sleep (5.0s) with a wide margin rather than a 1.0s/0.5s wall-clock bound. Keep the async-vs-blocking distinction: the stub sleeps 5.0s, so a 2.5-3.0s ceiling still catches a synchronous join while being load-robust.

REGRESSION: run the two tests under a saturated host (bounded loadgen / competing full-suite run) and assert they pass; and keep them failing when the async dispatch is made synchronous.
foreman_note: PASS faf17d52 (tier1+tier2, no skipped steps). tests/test_mcp_server.py +25/-7: file-owned CI_GENEROUS_ASYNC_SECONDS=3.0 replaces elapsed<1.0 and elapsed<0.5; task.complete stub raised to sleep=5.0 with 15s poll deadline so the ceiling keeps teeth against a sync join; mutation check (dispatch made synchronous) failed both tests at 5.15s; target tests 5x green; full suite 2100/16 on the branch.

title: Process gap - serialize `gitreins task complete`: parallel Tier-2 judges share .gitreins/tasks.yaml and corrupt it (one judge loses its task, .corrupt-* copies appear)
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-21 foreman tick (wave of 3). Three `gitreins task complete` runs were launched concurrently for DF-GITREINS-POC-30/-31/-32 (wave closure).

MEASURED: one run aborted with `Task not found: DF-GITREINS-POC-32` after printing `Warning: failed to load tasks: while scanning a simple key in ".../.gitreins/tasks.yaml", line 810`; another printed `Warning: ... looks truncated ... preserved the unreadable task state as .../tasks.yaml.corrupt-789a505a4717`. Two `.corrupt-*` files appeared (57,314 bytes unparsable; 0 bytes). The live file itself survived (142 tasks, valid YAML) and the affected task completed after a serial rerun.

WHY IT MATTERS: task state is read-modify-write on one shared path. A wave tick (the normal case for this repo, up to 12 workers) naturally wants N judges at once, so the corruption is the default behaviour, not an edge case: a judge can silently grade nothing, and a `task complete` that never ran is indistinguishable from one that passed if the tick only reads status.

FIX DIRECTION (either): (a) a lock file around the tasks.yaml read-modify-write (the reserve step already treats the store as shared state), or (b) foreman doctrine + a helper that runs `task complete` serially for a wave while the workers themselves stay parallel — the AC here is that concurrent completes cannot interleave a write.

REGRESSION: a test that issues two concurrent completes (or two concurrent load-modify-save cycles) and asserts the final file parses AND contains both tasks.
foreman_note: PASS 229889ca (tier1+tier2, no skipped steps). engine/task_manager.py: _locked_load_save funnels create/start/complete/delete through one fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on sidecar .gitreins/tasks.yaml.lock, reload-mutate-save inside the lock, atomic temp-file os.replace; new tests/test_task_manager_concurrency.py (5 tests, multiprocessing fork: 2-proc race + 4x5 stress) proves concurrent completes land both tasks with no .corrupt sidecars; docs counts 2116/57 -> 2121/58 (README x2 + CONTRIBUTING x2).

title: CI flake - test_mcp_verdict_persistence.py::TestCliUsesSharedHelper::test_cli_skips_persistence_when_history_disabled fails on py3.11 only and passes on rerun (step-level red on a board-only commit)
detail:
FOUND 2026-09-21 foreman tick (wave of 3), observed on my own board commit b4c298d ('board: close wave manifest ...', a JSON manifest only — no source change).

MEASURED: GitHub run 35567074008, SHA b4c298d, job test (3.11) -> step 'Run tests' FAILURE; jobs test (3.10) and test (3.12) on the SAME SHA -> success. Failure:
  FAILED tests/test_mcp_verdict_persistence.py::TestCliUsesSharedHelper::test_cli_skips_persistence_when_history_disabled
  AssertionError: enabled history must persist through the shared helper
  assert 2 == 1
with the accompanying non-fatal log line 'Failed to persist verdict for /tmp/pytest-of-runner/... : '_FakeJudgeResult' object has no attribute 'verdict''.

This is CI-law relevant under the 09-19 doctrine: steps>0 means REAL failure (not an infra/billing block), so it is filed rather than deduped. Honest scope: the test file has an EMPTY diff across the whole tick (afe6467..a58c36e), the code-paths it exercises were not touched, two of three Python versions passed on the same SHA, and `gh run rerun 35567074008 --failed` returned SUCCESS for the same SHA — so this is flake evidence, not a regression. It still matters because it can red main on a no-op commit and burn a triage.

SUSPECTED MECHANISM (to confirm, not assumed): `assert len(calls) == 1` counts calls made through a monkeypatched spy on engine.persist.persist_evaluation — a call-count assertion, which the same test's own docstring says it moved away from ('asserting the artefact rather than a call count, so neither arm can pass vacuously'). The observed '2 == 1' means the spy saw a second call, consistent with leaking state between the two arms / another test's persistence path under xdist (arm 1 calls the real helper, which itself may re-enter).

FIX DIRECTION: make both arms assert the artefact only (verdict file count, which the test already checks) and drop the call-count assertion, or scope the spy so no cross-test/arm leakage is possible; then run the file repeatedly under xdist to show stability.

REGRESSION: the two arms pass in a loop (e.g. -k with xdist, N repetitions) on all three Pythons.
foreman_note: PASS 185243a7 (tier1+tier2, no skipped steps). tests/test_mcp_verdict_persistence.py: spy and monkeypatch removed, both arms assert the on-disk verdict-file artefact only (entry dirs are microsecond-stamped so any real or leaked persist moves the count); 5x sequential green, whole file green under -n 2; full suite 2100/16 on the branch.

title: [P2] guard hook_timeout early-return drops allow_skips: a slow repo's docs/board commits are BLOCKED (exit 2) by a run whose own warning says 'commit allowed to proceed'
foreman_note: PASS 7622886c (tier1+tier2, 3/3 criteria). Worker hit provider exhaustion; foreman-direct fixup: _timeout_result() helper replaces all 10 timeout early-returns; 6 tests (deterministic clock + real-clock test_on_clean); test-count synced 2195->2203. RELEASE-003 blocker cleared.
reasoning: Measured in /home/kara/auger this tick (2026-09-21, gitreins 0.14.0). engine/guard_manager.py run_all() checks _timed_out() after each arm and early-returns Tier1Result(passed=True, results=results, warnings=warnings) with the warning 'Guard timed out after <hook_timeout>s (hook_timeout). Remaining checks skipped — commit allowed to proceed (fail-open).' That Tier1Result has NO extra map, so extra['allow_skips'] is absent. gitreins/cli.py cmd_guard_run (~line 2038) does: if result.degraded and not result.extra.get('allow_skips', False): print the DEGRADED PASS warning and sys.exit(2). The two statements CONTRADICT each other: the guard announces the commit is allowed and then the CLI exits 2, which the pre-commit hook propagates, so the commit is BLOCKED. Reproduction: repo with guards.allow_skips: true and a tests arm whose runtime exceeds hook_timeout (auger: test_command 'bash tests/gate.sh' takes 250-420s, hook_timeout default 300) -> 'git commit' of a board/docs-only change exits 1 with 'Guard timed out after 300s (hook_timeout) ... DEGRADED PASS: lint=no staged files', no gate ever failing. Evidence: auger tick auger-2026-09-21-11-30-00; guard log .gitreins/logs/guard-20260921T124407.813683Z.log. Two candidate fixes (pick one, both defensible): (a) the timeout early-return should build its Tier1Result with the same extra map as the normal exit path so allow_skips is honoured and the documented fail-open behaviour is real; and/or (b) a timeout is not a skip — a DEGRADED run caused by the overall budget should be reported as its own outcome (e.g. incomplete/not-evidence) rather than reusing the zero-work-skip exit policy, so the failing-repo distinction survives. Whichever is chosen, the CLI warning text and the exit code must agree. Acceptance: a repo with allow_skips:true and a tests arm that exceeds hook_timeout can commit a docs-only change with the timeout warning printed and exit 0; and a repo with allow_skips:false (or a genuinely failing arm) still exits non-zero. Also worth a default bump: hook_timeout 300 < the 600 test_timeout default shipped in the same file, so any repo that raises test_timeout above 300 silently loses its tests arm.
